interactions.title: The Crown's complete mirror vision
lines: DM: So Kenzo holds the crown up to the mirror.
Kenzo: Like close to his head, but not not on it.

DM: Yeah, common. It's strange. When you pick it up, it seems to recoil from your touch. You feel, like, a sort of sparkling, almost a magnetic repulsion as you try and hold on. It seems once you have lost it, it is—
DM: And you look in the mirror, and it shows you—the 1st thing you see is a study. It looks maybe Chardonian some time ago, maybe a hundred years. It's hard to say.
Delwath: This is probably Fausto finding it.

DM: Maybe a hundred 50 years, and you see— and it seems what the, the crown itself looks not like it looks now, the Riswynn crown, nor like the Fausto crown. It is a plain, like, wooden band. No decoration, nothing.

DM: You're in a study, and somebody looks like they are, you know, doing research, cataloging things? There is on their desk what seems to be the beginnings of a treatise on the historical greatness of Drankor. How can—how to bring back the might of empire? Somebody seems obsessed. You see notes scattered across the page, like 'Apollyon,' like 'scepter lost, cloak lost. Could this be the crown?'

DM: And then you see hands gripping it, and time speed seems to speed up slightly as first there's this electric shock, and the person who was holding it seems to fall dead, and somebody else walks in, somebody older, seeming to be like the master, the leader of whatever this group is, smiling as he reaches and grabs the crown, and it shifts and elongates the 4 points of Fausto's crown beginning to form.
Delwath: But this person's not Fausto? We can't—
DM: Not Fausto. They were old when they picked up the crown, so must have passed on. Whoever this was was the person who founded the cult.

DM: And then the scene shifts, time reversing, going backwards, the plain wooden band sitting dusty in a forgotten chest, not even radiating magic, lost going back and back and back, part of a a caravan traveling across Dunmar in a chest tossed carelessly, now not wooden but an iron band tossed with dozens of other meaningless Drankorian artifacts. Are there iron bands, going back further and further buried underground.

DM: And then you see Apollyon standing in life, standing in front of the doors to this temple, wearing the crown, holding out the scepter as bands of magic fly from him towards Cha'mutte, flying in the sky above him, and as Cha'mutte breathes and rends, the red mist piles around Apollyon. Strand after strand after strand, hundreds of strands break, thousands of strands break. It must be 5, 6, 7, 8,000 people in command of Apollyon through this crown die and die and die and die, until finally there are none left, and Apollyon screams in frustration and in desperation grabs a vial of black liquid from his pouch, and drinks it as the walls of his temple seal up around him, and the crown is tossed from his head across Drankor, skipping, and time jumps suddenly back, a long time back.
DM: You don't ever see how Apollyon found it. Back to Hkar.

DM: The Great War, people terrified, a giant armada bearing down on the island. Nobody's sure what to do. The crown sitting again now a plain iron band on a marble table in a temple. Some discussion around murmured low voices in a language you do not understand. You can't hear anything anyway.

DM: And then nodding, and one of the men and women gathered here reaches for the crown and grabs it and puts it on their head, and lines of power shoot out, and again time sort of speeds up and reverses. And you see the crown reaching out with these 12 people together, and the island breaks apart and begins to walk.
Delwath: Yeah, because the crown made it walk. That's pretty cool.

DM: And then flying back even further, drifting far, far, far back into time, before humans even existed, back to that, the forests of the elves, back to when the gods strode through the world, the days of myth, when the foot—when the footsteps of the gods reshaped the world itself, the Plane of Magic intertwined, the Plane of Souls intertwined with the world itself, and then a shattering.

DM: The moment when the gods pulled the, the world apart, and something was caught when the world was pulled apart and curled itself into a circlet and fell into the forest. A fragment of the ancient days when the world could be reshaped, frozen in material form, mindless but powerful, waiting, a chameleon always to adapt to whoever puts it on, and the mirror goes black.

interactions.title: Interpreting the Crown and its moral cost
lines: Delwath: Okay, okay. So the vision ends.
Kenzo: Kenzo's currently holding the crown, and he, he starts to give it back to Wellby.

Riswynn: This essentially, and somewhere, under some amount of dirt or not, a circlet forms somewhere on the, in some plane of Taelgar, and somewhere surface. But it won't be our problem.
Seeker: Wait, Tim, I have a question. Are there—is there some a unique phenomenon in the universe? Or are there other items that have this kind of history and provenance?

DM: You've never heard of anything like—I mean, this is like, so the reading this thing you saw is like when the multiverse was created. There's nothing—no lore suggests that there are, like, many items that survive from that moment, right? This is for sure unique.

Delwath: No, no, no, it's not a scholarly argument at all, Seeker. I mean, something like this is not to be given to a scholar. I can't— it's too— powerful, and I think a scholar is too unfocused and unintentional about their acts.

Wellby: This ring is a gift? You're saying we should use it?

Riswynn: But my argument is, we just came through a moment in history, where, through our training and our partnership and our devotions to our various studies and and skills, we have just averted the worst case in our time frame, and the next noble quest of like some number of months to years of like cleanup of like hench people is not the noble quest that this crown must— or else humanity fail. Like, it's just, like, it'll take us months or take us 4 months.

We disappeared it from abuse for our for our moment, and I think that's what's good.
Delwath: No, no, no, no, no! Sorry! I mean, there's nothing in its history that suggests its use is corrupting.

Delwath: But I was wrong, Kenzo.
Kenzo: Oh, you were wrong! Oh, that's so, so—
Delwath: I already told you that.
Kenzo: That's so amusing that you're wrong.
Wellby: It doesn't need to be corrupting to be too powerful. It shouldn't ever have been in this world. It wasn't given to mortals to have the ability to reshape this place.

Riswynn: I do think it was given to certain times and places to reshape this place. It's like that's its existence. But right now it's not—right now it's not cleanly—if it fell out of the sky right now after some period of total disuse, and we recognized it as a virgin circlet of wood or iron that it manifested as, with no poor 93 Chardonians attached to it with no free will or minimum minimized free will, who can never be reset by the will—
Riswynn: Yes, I can't let them free.
DM: I mean, you've been attuned to it for 4 days. Who knows what you could do if you were attuned to it for months.
Riswynn: I think I thought that I had to, that I couldn't let them free, and so I had to throw it to do a reset to get free.

DM: You don't have the power to set them free right now. That doesn't necessarily mean the crown is not able to set them. It clearly grows more. I mean— there's a lot you don't know. There's a lot you are unable to do, right? Basically, you're just taking over what Fausto was doing.
Delwath: But wait. Do we have any— I mean, I guess it's hard to know. We don't know. Do you—does the mirror—does the crown only work by taking over people's free will? That wasn't—
Delwath: Yeah, that wasn't the impression I got.
Riswynn: But it worked by taking over people's free will for Apollyon, and then Fausto, and then, and the dude before Fausto, whose name we don't know or care about.

Delwath: So why so certain that there is nobody who could do great good to balance the great evil that will surely come in the future? Why hide it when the only—when surely the only true, honest thing to do with something like this is to use it? If anybody felt they could achieve great good, because otherwise only those seeking evil will use it. Hiding it doesn't prevent another being used.
Seeker: What if there's another path, a way to hold it in reserve in a way where we do our best to make sure that it can only be unlocked in some deep future time by someone with good intentions?
